+    "BreakEven",
+    "Edge",
+    "Mixture",
+    "NotComparable",
+    "NotComparableReason",
+    "priced",
+]

class World(BaseModel):
    """One finished answer: a map, the values its edits fixed, and every number worked through.

    A world is a **computed result, never a source of truth**. It can always be
    thrown away and rebuilt from three things — the base map, the branch and the
    seed — and if a stored world ever disagrees with what those three produce, the
    stored world is the one that is wrong.

    Every likelihood in `beliefs` is owned by the model and is read on that claim's
    own resolve-by day, which is the day the claim is judged and the date its tile
    already shows. `series` carries one likelihood per day so the spike and the
    fade are visible rather than hidden, and `states` says, for each of those days,
    whether the number is the ordinary sampled one, a supposition holding, a
    supposition withdrawn with no push yet, or a push that has landed.

    **A claim whose supposition is holding reads 1 — exactly 1, range and all, or
    0 when it was supposed false.** That number is there so that a chain of claims
    multiplied together has a factor for it, and for nothing else: **no surface may
    print it.** Every reader looks at `states` first and prints the word *Supposed*
    where the number would go, because "suppose this is true" answered with a
    likelihood is a tool arguing with the person using it.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    base_id: str = Field(description="The map this world was built from.")
    branch_id: BranchId | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The branch that was folded on. None means the base world, the empty branch. "
            "Working the numbers through takes a map and the values its edits fixed, and "
            "never the branch itself, so whatever asked for the world writes this in."
        ),
    )
    seed: int = Field(description="The one number every random draw in here came from.")
    versions: int = Field(
        description="The outer loop: how many versions of the map were tried — how sure we are "
        "of the numbers we put in."
    )
    worlds: int = Field(
        description="The inner loop: how many worlds were run under each version — how the "
        "dice fall."
    )
    day_zero: date = Field(description="The day the window starts on.")
    days: int = Field(
        description=(
            "How long the window is, in whole days. Not the number of points in a series: "
            "past 180 days a series is drawn at 180 evenly spaced points, plus every claim's "
            "own resolve-by day, which is always kept."
        )
    )
    graph: Graph = Field(description="The map the branch's edits left behind.")
    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...] = Field(
        description="Every value an edit fixed, in the order the edits were made."
    )
    retractions: tuple[Retraction, ...] = Field(
        description="Every supposition that a later edit undermined, and what undermined it."
    )
    beliefs: Mapping[PropositionId, Belief] = Field(
        description=(
            "The model's likelihood for each claim, read on that claim's own resolve-by "
            "day, with the range that says how sure we are of it."
        )
    )
    series_days: tuple[int, ...] = Field(
        description=(
            "Which day of the window each point of every series stands for, counting from "
            "zero. Ordinarily every day. Past 180 days the series is drawn at fewer, "
            "unevenly spaced days — every claim's own resolve-by day is always among them, "
            "so a tile's headline number is always a point of the line drawn beneath it — "
            "and then this is the only thing that says where those points sit."
        )
    )
    series: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[float, ...]] = Field(
        description=("One likelihood for each of the days above, for the scrubbable time axis.")
    )
    states: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[SeriesState, ...]] = Field(
        description="One named state per day, the same length as the series."
    )
    conditionals: Mapping[LinkId, Belief] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "The likelihood of an arrow's target with that arrow's source **supposed** "
            "true — never how often the two show up together. Empty on a freshly built "
            "world: it costs a whole extra run per arrow, so it is fetched one arrow at "
            "a time when something asks."
        ),
    )
    range_shares: Mapping[PropositionId, Mapping[PropositionId, float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "How much of each claim's band comes from not being sure of each claim's "
            "prior: range_shares[target][source]. Nothing on screen reads it yet; it is "
            "carried because the sample it comes from is thrown away otherwise."
        ),
    )
    warnings: tuple[str, ...] = Field(
        default=(),
        description="Plain sentences the reader should see under the map.",

"""Work every row of the edge decision table by hand and compare with `priced`.

Run from the worktree's backend:

    cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend && \
      env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run --no-sync python \
      /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/06-1-review/table_by_hand.py

Nothing here is typed except prices a venue could plausibly show. Every model
number is read out of the world the script builds, and every expected answer is
worked out in this file from those numbers rather than copied from the code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, date, datetime

from katalyst.domain import (
    Belief,
    Beliefs,
    Branch,
    ContractPayoff,
    Do,
    Graph,
    Insert,
    Link,
    Observe,
    PricePayoff,
    Proposition,
    Resolution,
    Retune,
    Source,
    World,
    apply,
    introduced_by,
    propagate,
)
from katalyst.grounding import Quote
from katalyst.thesis import Edge, NotComparable, priced

DAY_ZERO = date(2026, 1, 1)
SMALL = {"versions": 16, "worlds": 4}
INSTANT = datetime(2026, 9, 21, 14, 48, 27, tzinfo=UTC)
WIDE = Belief(p=0.35, lo=0.22, hi=0.50, owner="model")

failures: list[str] = []


def check(name: str, got: object, wanted: object) -> None:
    ok = got == wanted
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}: got {got!r}, wanted {wanted!r}")
    if not ok:
        failures.append(name)


def resolution() -> Resolution:
    return Resolution(
        criteria="A counted threshold over a named window.",
        source="The publisher of that number.",
        by=date(2026, 11, 1),
    )


def claim(identifier: str, kind: str, payoff: object = None, reason: str | None = None):
    return Proposition(
        id=identifier,
        claim=f"The claim called {identifier} comes out true.",
        kind=kind,
        resolution=resolution(),
        prior=WIDE,
        beliefs=Beliefs(model=WIDE),
        payoff=payoff,
        not_tradeable_reason=reason,
    )


YES = ContractPayoff(venue="Polymarket", contract_id="3501950", title="Does it?", side="yes")
NO = ContractPayoff(venue="Polymarket", contract_id="3501950", title="Does it?", side="no")
INSTRUMENT = PricePayoff(instrument="the front-month future", direction="short", move=0.03)


def the_map() -> Graph:
    return Graph(
        id="by-hand",
        hypothesis_id="start",
        propositions=(
            claim("start", "hypothesis"),
            claim("step", "event"),
            claim("yes_side", "market", payoff=YES),
            claim("no_side", "market", payoff=NO),
            claim("instrument", "market", payoff=INSTRUMENT),
            claim("untradeable", "not_tradeable", reason="Everything that would express it settles too late."),
        ),
        links=(
            Link(
                id="start-to-step",
                source="start",
                target="step",
                mode="trigger",
                strength=1.2,
                lag=3.0,
                shape="step",
                half_life=None,
                rationale="The step follows from the start.",
                sources=(Source(url="https://example.test/doc", title="A document"),),
                provenance="documented",
                reflexive=False,
            ),
            Link(
                id="step-to-yes",
                source="step",
                target="yes_side",
                mode="trigger",
                strength=0.9,
                lag=1.0,
                shape="step",
                half_life=None,
                rationale="The contract settles on the step.",
                sources=(),
                provenance="argued",
                reflexive=False,
            ),
        ),
    )


def world_of(graph: Graph, branch: Branch | None = None, seed: int = 1) -> World:
    folded = apply(graph, branch) if branch is not None else (graph, ())
    assert not isinstance(folded, list), folded
    left, fixed = folded
    world = propagate(
        left,
        fixed,
        as_of=DAY_ZERO,
        seed=seed,
        introduced_by=introduced_by(branch) if branch is not None else {},
        **SMALL,
    )
    return world.model_copy(update={"branch_id": branch.id if branch is not None else None})


def a_quote(bid: float, offer: float, *, side: str = "yes", live: bool = True) -> Quote:
    return Quote(
        bid=bid,
        offer=offer,
        as_of=INSTANT,
        source="recorded",
        closed=not live,
        accepting_orders=live,
        venue="Polymarket",
        condition_id="0xcontract",
        market_id="3501950",
        token_id="the-token",
        side=side,
        question="Does it?",
        rules="The venue's own rules.",
        ends=date(2026, 11, 1),
        tick=0.01,
        minimum_order=5.0,

"""Work every row of the edge decision table by hand and compare with `priced`.

Run from the worktree's backend:

    cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend && \
      env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run --no-sync python \
      /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/06-1-review/table_by_hand.py

Nothing here is typed except prices a venue could plausibly show. Every model
number is read out of the world the script builds, and every expected answer is
worked out in this file from those numbers rather than copied from the code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, date, datetime

from katalyst.domain import (
    Belief,
    Beliefs,
    Branch,
    ContractPayoff,
    Do,
    Graph,
    Insert,
    Link,
    Observe,
    PricePayoff,
    Proposition,
    Resolution,
    Retune,
    Source,
    World,
    apply,
    introduced_by,
    propagate,
)
from katalyst.grounding import Quote
from katalyst.thesis import Edge, NotComparable, priced

DAY_ZERO = date(2026, 1, 1)
SMALL = {"versions": 16, "worlds": 4}
INSTANT = datetime(2026, 9, 21, 14, 48, 27, tzinfo=UTC)
WIDE = Belief(p=0.35, lo=0.22, hi=0.50, owner="model")

failures: list[str] = []


def check(name: str, got: object, wanted: object) -> None:
    ok = got == wanted
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}: got {got!r}, wanted {wanted!r}")
    if not ok:
        failures.append(name)


def resolution() -> Resolution:
    return Resolution(
        criteria="A counted threshold over a named window.",
        source="The publisher of that number.",
        by=date(2026, 11, 1),
    )


def claim(identifier: str, kind: str, payoff: object = None, reason: str | None = None):
    return Proposition(
        id=identifier,
        claim=f"The claim called {identifier} comes out true.",
        kind=kind,
        resolution=resolution(),
        prior=WIDE,
        beliefs=Beliefs(model=WIDE),
        payoff=payoff,
        not_tradeable_reason=reason,
    )


YES = ContractPayoff(venue="Polymarket", contract_id="3501950", title="Does it?", side="yes")
NO = ContractPayoff(venue="Polymarket", contract_id="3501950", title="Does it?", side="no")
INSTRUMENT = PricePayoff(instrument="the front-month future", direction="short", move=0.03)


def the_map() -> Graph:
    return Graph(
        id="by-hand",
        hypothesis_id="start",
        propositions=(
            claim("start", "hypothesis"),
            claim("step", "event"),
            claim("yes_side", "market", payoff=YES),
            claim("no_side", "market", payoff=NO),
            claim("instrument", "market", payoff=INSTRUMENT),
            claim("untradeable", "not_tradeable", reason="Everything that would express it settles too late."),
        ),
        links=(
            Link(
                id="start-to-step",
                source="start",
                target="step",
                mode="trigger",
                strength=1.2,
                lag=3.0,
                shape="step",
                half_life=None,
                rationale="The step follows from the start.",
                sources=(Source(url="https://example.test/doc", title="A document"),),
                provenance="documented",
                reflexive=False,
            ),
            Link(
                id="step-to-yes",
                source="step",
                target="yes_side",
                mode="trigger",
                strength=0.9,
                lag=1.0,
                shape="step",
                half_life=None,
                rationale="The contract settles on the step.",
                sources=(),
                provenance="argued",
                reflexive=False,
            ),
        ),
    )


def world_of(graph: Graph, branch: Branch | None = None, seed: int = 1) -> World:
    folded = apply(graph, branch) if branch is not None else (graph, ())
    assert not isinstance(folded, list), folded
    left, fixed = folded
    world = propagate(
        left,
        fixed,
        as_of=DAY_ZERO,
        seed=seed,
        introduced_by=introduced_by(branch) if branch is not None else {},
        **SMALL,
    )
    return world.model_copy(update={"branch_id": branch.id if branch is not None else None})


def a_quote(bid: float, offer: float, *, side: str = "yes", live: bool = True) -> Quote:
    return Quote(
        bid=bid,
        offer=offer,
        as_of=INSTANT,
        source="recorded",
        closed=not live,
        accepting_orders=live,
        venue="Polymarket",
        condition_id="0xcontract",
        market_id="3501950",
        token_id="the-token",
        side=side,
        question="Does it?",
        rules="The venue's own rules.",
        ends=date(2026, 11, 1),
        tick=0.01,
        minimum_order=5.0,
        resting=119_187.28,
        traded=754_974.31,
        url="https://example.test/event/does-it",
    )


def main() -> None:
    graph = the_map()
    base = world_of(graph)
    model = base.beliefs["yes_side"]
    print(f"\nthe model's number for yes_side, read from the world: p={model.p!r} "
          f"lo={model.lo!r} hi={model.hi!r}\n")

    # --- 1. a buy: the model above the offer -------------------------------
    offer, bid, fee = round(model.p - 0.10, 4), round(model.p - 0.12, 4), 0.02
    answer = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(bid, offer), fee=fee)
    assert isinstance(answer, Edge)
    check("buy: edge of buying = model - offer - fee", answer.buying, model.p - offer - fee)
    check("buy: edge of selling = bid - model - fee", answer.selling, bid - model.p - fee)
    check("buy: buying is the positive side", (answer.buying > 0, answer.selling > 0), (True, False))
    check("buy: break-even buy_below = model - fee", answer.break_even.buy_below, model.p - fee)
    check("buy: break-even sell_above = model + fee", answer.break_even.sell_above, model.p + fee)

    # --- 2. a sell: the model below the bid --------------------------------
    bid, offer = round(model.p + 0.12, 4), round(model.p + 0.14, 4)
    answer = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(bid, offer), fee=fee)
    assert isinstance(answer, Edge)
    check("sell: edge of selling = bid - model - fee", answer.selling, bid - model.p - fee)
    check("sell: selling is the positive side", (answer.buying > 0, answer.selling > 0), (False, True))

    # --- 3. inside the spread: neither side --------------------------------
    bid, offer = round(model.p - 0.03, 4), round(model.p + 0.03, 4)
    answer = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(bid, offer), fee=0.0)
    assert isinstance(answer, Edge)
    check("inside the spread: neither edge is positive",
          (answer.buying > 0, answer.selling > 0), (False, False))
    check("inside the spread: nothing is compared with the midpoint",
          answer.buying == model.p - answer.quote.midpoint, False)

    # --- 4. with and without a fee -----------------------------------------
    without = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(bid, offer), fee=0.0)
    withfee = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(bid, offer), fee=0.03)
    assert isinstance(without, Edge) and isinstance(withfee, Edge)
    check("a fee takes the same amount off both sides",
          (round(without.buying - withfee.buying, 12), round(without.selling - withfee.selling, 12)),
          (0.03, 0.03))
    check("no fee given at all is the same as a zero fee",
          priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(bid, offer)), without)

    # --- 5. the not-ranked rule, at both ends, against the right price -----
    middle = (model.lo + model.hi) / 2.0
    straddling = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(middle, middle), fee=0.0)
    assert isinstance(straddling, Edge)
    by_hand_buy = ((model.lo - middle < 0.0) != (model.hi - middle < 0.0))
    by_hand_sell = ((middle - model.lo < 0.0) != (middle - model.hi < 0.0))
    check("not ranked: the flag is set when the price sits inside the range",
          straddling.inside_the_model_range, True)
    check("not ranked: by hand, buying changes sign across the range", by_hand_buy, True)
    check("not ranked: by hand, selling changes sign across the range", by_hand_sell, True)

    # A price OUTSIDE the range on the buying side, but a bid that straddles it.
    # Buying is worth it at both ends; selling changes sign. The flag must be set.
    one_sided = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(middle, round(model.lo - 0.05, 4)), fee=0.0)
    assert isinstance(one_sided, Edge)
    check("not ranked: a bid inside the range alone still marks it",
          one_sided.inside_the_model_range, True)

    outside = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(0.0, 0.0), fee=0.0)
    assert isinstance(outside, Edge)
    check("not ranked: a price below the whole range is not marked",
          outside.inside_the_model_range, False)

    # --- 6. a no-side contract payoff --------------------------------------
    # The claim's own number is the chance the claim comes TRUE. The `no` token
    # pays when it FAILS, so the number to compare a no-token price with is
    # 1 - model.p. Buying NO at .60 when the model says the claim is .35 true
    # (so .65 false) is worth .65 - .60 = +.05.
    no_offer, no_bid = 0.60, 0.58
    honest_buying_no = (1.0 - model.p) - no_offer
    answer = priced(base, base, "no_side", a_quote(no_bid, no_offer, side="no"), fee=0.0)
    assert isinstance(answer, Edge)
    print(f"\n  no-side: the model says the claim is {model.p!r} true, so {1.0 - model.p!r} false.")
    print(f"  the NO token is offered at {no_offer} and bid at {no_bid}.")
    print(f"  buying the NO token is worth {honest_buying_no!r} by hand;")
    print(f"  `priced` reports buying = {answer.buying!r}, selling = {answer.selling!r}.")
    check("no side: the edge of buying is worked out on the side that was priced",
          round(answer.buying, 12), round(honest_buying_no, 12))
    check("no side: the quote's own side reaches the edge at all",
          answer.quote.side, "no")

    # A quote for the WRONG side of the same contract, handed to a yes-side ending.
    crossed = priced(base, base, "yes_side", a_quote(no_bid, no_offer, side="no"), fee=0.0)
    check("a quote for the other side of the contract is refused",
          isinstance(crossed, NotComparable), True)

    # A quote for a DIFFERENT market entirely.
    elsewhere = a_quote(0.90, 0.92).model_copy(update={"market_id": "7654321"})
    other = priced(base, base, "yes_side", elsewhere, fee=0.0)
    check("a quote for another market is refused", isinstance(other, NotComparable), True)

    # --- 7. the other rows of the table ------------------------------------
    live = a_quote(round(model.p - 0.10, 4), round(model.p - 0.08, 4))
    settled = a_quote(0.999, 1.0, live=False)
    rows = {
        "the hypothesis": priced(base, base, "start", live),
        "a step in the middle": priced(base, base, "step", live),
        "a not-tradeable ending": priced(base, base, "untradeable", live),
        "an instrument ending": priced(base, base, "instrument", live),
        "an instrument ending with no quote": priced(base, base, "instrument", None),
        "a contract with no quote": priced(base, base, "yes_side", None),
        "a settled market": priced(base, base, "yes_side", settled),
    }
    for name, got in rows.items():
        assert isinstance(got, NotComparable), (name, got)
        print(f"  {name}: {got.reason}, break-even "
              f"{'yes' if got.break_even is not None else 'no'}")
    check("hypothesis -> no_contract, no break-even",
          (rows["the hypothesis"].reason, rows["the hypothesis"].break_even), ("no_contract", None))
    check("step -> no_contract", rows["a step in the middle"].reason, "no_contract")
    check("not-tradeable -> its own stored reason",
          rows["a not-tradeable ending"].sentence,
          "Everything that would express it settles too late.")
    check("instrument -> no_contract, no break-even",
          (rows["an instrument ending"].reason, rows["an instrument ending"].break_even),
          ("no_contract", None))
    check("contract, no quote -> no_quote with the break-even",
          (rows["a contract with no quote"].reason,
           rows["a contract with no quote"].break_even.buy_below),
          ("no_quote", model.p))
    check("settled -> settled_market with the break-even",
          (rows["a settled market"].reason, rows["a settled market"].break_even.buy_below),
          ("settled_market", model.p))

    # --- 8. R20: which edits refuse ----------------------------------------
    for name, edit in (
        ("Suppose this is true", Do(target="step", value=True)),
        ("Suppose false", Do(target="step", value=False)),
        ("This happened", Observe(target="step", value=True)),
    ):
        world = world_of(graph, Branch(id="b", label=name, interventions=(edit,)))
        got = priced(world, world, "yes_side", live)
        check(f"R20: {name} refuses", isinstance(got, NotComparable) and got.reason, "conditional_world")

    inserted = Branch(
        id="b",
        label="insert",
        interventions=(
            Insert(
                proposition=claim("added", "event"),
                links=(
                    Link(
                        id="added-to-step",
                        source="added",
                        target="step",
                        mode="trigger",
                        strength=0.8,
                        lag=2.0,
                        shape="step",
                        half_life=None,
                        rationale="The added claim pushes the step.",
                        sources=(),
                        provenance="argued",
                        reflexive=False,
                    ),
                ),
            ),
        ),
    )
    world = world_of(graph, inserted)
    got = priced(world, world, "yes_side", live)
    check("R20: an inserted claim is accepted", isinstance(got, Edge), True)

    retuned = Branch(
        id="b", label="retune", interventions=(Retune(link_id="step-to-yes", strength=2.5),)
    )
    world = world_of(graph, retuned)
    got = priced(world, world, "yes_side", live)
    print(f"  a retuned arrow: {type(got).__name__}"
          + (f" ({got.reason})" if isinstance(got, NotComparable) else ""))
    if isinstance(got, Edge):
        print(f"    and the number it priced is {got.model.p!r}, "
              f"against the untouched map's {base.beliefs['yes_side'].p!r}")
        check("R20: a retuned arrow gives an edge on the RETUNED number",
              got.model.p == base.beliefs["yes_side"].p, True)

    # --- 9. base and shown from different maps -----------------------------
    other_graph = the_map().model_copy(update={"id": "another-map"})
    other_base = world_of(other_graph, seed=99)
    mixed = priced(base, other_base, "yes_side", live)
    check("base and shown from two different maps is accepted without a word",
          isinstance(mixed, Edge), True)

    print("\n" + ("ALL CHECKS PASSED" if not failures else f"FAILURES: {failures}"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def resolutions(draw: Any) -> Resolution:
    """How one claim gets settled: the test, the judge, and the date.

    Generates: a test and a judge drawn from short lists of realistic wordings, and
    a date.
    Guarantees: neither the test nor the judge is blank, which is what rule one asks
    for.
    """
    return Resolution(
        criteria=draw(st.sampled_from(CRITERIA_SENTENCES)),
        source=draw(st.sampled_from(ADJUDICATORS)),
        by=draw(st.dates(min_value=date(2026, 1, 1), max_value=date(2030, 12, 31))),
    )


@composite
def payoffs(draw: Any) -> Payoff:
    """What one tradeable ending is worth, either way round.

    Generates: half the time a named contract at a named venue and the side you
    would take; the other half an instrument, which way you would take it, and how
    far its price is expected to move.
    Guarantees: both arms are built, so anything reading a payoff is made to cope
    with both. A price move is never negative — the side carries the direction —
    and a contract always names the venue and the contract, so a reader can look it
    up. Neither arm says what the position costs; that is not this layer's business.
    """
    if draw(st.booleans()):
        return ContractPayoff(
            venue=draw(st.sampled_from(CONTRACT_VENUES)),
            contract_id=draw(st.sampled_from(("brent-below-seventy", "strait-open-fortnight"))),
            title=draw(st.sampled_from(CONTRACT_TITLES)),
            side=draw(st.sampled_from(("yes", "no"))),
        )
    return PricePayoff(
        instrument=draw(st.sampled_from(INSTRUMENTS)),
        direction=draw(st.sampled_from(("long", "short"))),
        move=draw(st.floats(min_value=0.0, max_value=3.0, allow_nan=False)),

1	# Quotes — where a price comes from, and what it has to say about itself
2	
3	## Purpose
4	
5	A price on this screen must say where it came from, when it was true, and how we got it. A reader can now see what a real venue is charging for a claim on the map, open the market to check, and know at a glance whether the number was read a moment ago, read from a committed file, or typed in by themselves.
6	
7	It also fixes a boundary: **a market price is a venue's number about a future claim; a measured economic level is an observation about the past.** They do not go in the same slot.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Data model
12	
13	`backend/src/katalyst/grounding/quote.py` holds **`Quote`**, the only shape allowed to carry a price. `recorded.py` loads one from the committed file, `polymarket.py` reads one from the venue when the reader asks, `fred.py` reads a spot level. Nothing in `domain/` gains a field.
14	
15	It stores **what the venue returned** and derives the rest:
16	
17	* **the venue and its three identifiers** — the on-chain condition identifier, the venue's market identifier, and the **outcome token identifier**, because only the token identifier buys a price: a contract's yes and no are two separate order books — and **the side** quoted, since the same contract can read `.07` on one side and `.93` on the other;
18	* **the best bid and best offer, as read.** The **midpoint** — halfway between them — and the cost of dealing are derived from these, never the other way round;
19	* **the instant it was true**, because the book moves within the day and the venue returns milliseconds. Store the instant, print the day;
20	* **resting size and traded volume**, because a midpoint over an empty book is a different claim from one over a hundred thousand dollars of resting orders; and **closed** and **accepting orders**, because a settled market keeps serving a book and live-or-settled is read from these, never from the price;
21	* **the venue's own question, resolution rules and end date**, so a reader can check the venue asks the same question with no network; and its **minimum price increment**, because a gap smaller than that is not tradeable;
22	* **a web address** that opens the market, and **`source`** — `fetched`, `recorded` or `user`, which the sentence on screen and the caveat in the export both need.
23	
24	**A reader's own price carries almost none of that** — a price, a date, free text for where they got it — and the absent fields stay absent rather than being invented. It is their *report of a price they could deal at*, which is not what they think the claim is worth: that is a `user` belief and it lives on the tile.
25	
26	A **spot anchor** is a separate, smaller shape in `fred.py`: a series name, a level, the date it is for, and the vintage. An observation, not a belief and not a quote.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Behaviour
31	
32	### B1 — Recorded first, fetched second
33	
34	A committed, dated file under `backend/recordings/quotes/`, named by the venue's market identifier, holds the quotes the worked example needs; continuous integration, the Docker build and the keyless walk read it and nothing else, and no test makes a network call. It is written by a command only the coordinator runs, and **its first line says why it is in the repository**: a dated quote kept for research and development (Kent's decision R23 of 2026-09-21).
35	
36	One route refreshes a quote — never on page load, never in a test, never in the build. **When it fails, the recorded quote stays and the card says the refresh failed**; the date on screen is still true. On the machine this was written on the refresh *will* fail, because the local resolver returns no address for the venue's hosts, which is why recorded-first is the rule rather than a fallback.
37	
38	### B2 — A price you typed
39	
40	A reader can type a price on any claim, on any map, with no venue and no key: *the best I can get is 41 cents* (**illustrative**). It is stamped `user`, dated, and printed as theirs; any edge against it carries *against a price you entered* on the same line. It does **not** fill the market chip on the tile, which says what a venue is charging (INV-11, three voices never merged).
41	
42	### B3 — What the venue quotes, on the worked maps
43	
44	Read from the venue on 2026-09-21 and saved raw; record 0020 has the detail. **Nothing quotes Brent crude**, so the curated map's Brent ending — and all eleven endings on the **recorded** map the walk opens — run on *no contract quotes this claim*, permanently.
45	
46	The venue does quote the curated map's **hypothesis**, with the same deadline and a different resolution test. Kent's decision R30 takes that test as the map's own and adds one ending of kind `market` naming the contract, so the **curated** fixture carries exactly one comparable venue price. The **recorded** map is untouched until the one paid re-recording after the freeze.
47	
48	### B4 — A market belief is a point, and the spread is a cost
49	
50	Where a venue quotes a claim, the midpoint becomes the `market` belief on the tile. It has **no range**: the venue publishes no interval, so the low and high ends equal the number, and the chip says in words that no interval was published rather than implying certainty. What the two sides of the book differ by is what dealing costs, and it shows up in the buying and selling edges. Turning a spread into a range, as an earlier draft of this product did, produces a number nobody can trace to an input, a rule or a source.
51	
52	### B5 — How a quote prints
53	
54	Never as a bare number. The venue, the value, how we got it and the day are one unit, in one type size:
55	
56	```
57	Polymarket · .07 · recorded 2026-09-21
58	```
59	
60	That value is real — the midpoint of the Hormuz contract, read at 14:48 UTC on 2026-09-21. When likelihoods move to a percentage form a contract price will print the same way, and the card keeps saying which it is: **a price is not a probability**, even where the two read the same. # Quotes — where a price comes from, and what it has to say about itself

## Purpose

A price on this screen must say where it came from, when it was true, and how we got it. A reader can now see what a real venue is charging for a claim on the map, open the market to check, and know at a glance whether the number was read a moment ago, read from a committed file, or typed in by themselves.

It also fixes a boundary: **a market price is a venue's number about a future claim; a measured economic level is an observation about the past.** They do not go in the same slot.

---

## Data model

`backend/src/katalyst/grounding/quote.py` holds **`Quote`**, the only shape allowed to carry a price. `recorded.py` loads one from the committed file, `polymarket.py` reads one from the venue when the reader asks, `fred.py` reads a spot level. Nothing in `domain/` gains a field.

It stores **what the venue returned** and derives the rest:

* **the venue and its three identifiers** — the on-chain condition identifier, the venue's market identifier, and the **outcome token identifier**, because only the token identifier buys a price: a contract's yes and no are two separate order books — and **the side** quoted, since the same contract can read `.07` on one side and `.93` on the other;
* **the best bid and best offer, as read.** The **midpoint** — halfway between them — and the cost of dealing are derived from these, never the other way round;
* **the instant it was true**, because the book moves within the day and the venue returns milliseconds. Store the instant, print the day;
* **resting size and traded volume**, because a midpoint over an empty book is a different claim from one over a hundred thousand dollars of resting orders; and **closed** and **accepting orders**, because a settled market keeps serving a book and live-or-settled is read from these, never from the price;
* **the venue's own question, resolution rules and end date**, so a reader can check the venue asks the same question with no network; and its **minimum price increment**, because a gap smaller than that is not tradeable;
* **a web address** that opens the market, and **`source`** — `fetched`, `recorded` or `user`, which the sentence on screen and the caveat in the export both need.

**A reader's own price carries almost none of that** — a price, a date, free text for where they got it — and the absent fields stay absent rather than being invented. It is their *report of a price they could deal at*, which is not what they think the claim is worth: that is a `user` belief and it lives on the tile.

A **spot anchor** is a separate, smaller shape in `fred.py`: a series name, a level, the date it is for, and the vintage. An observation, not a belief and not a quote.

---

## Behaviour

### B1 — Recorded first, fetched second

A committed, dated file under `backend/recordings/quotes/`, named by the venue's market identifier, holds the quotes the worked example needs; continuous integration, the Docker build and the keyless walk read it and nothing else, and no test makes a network call. It is written by a command only the coordinator runs, and **its first line says why it is in the repository**: a dated quote kept for research and development (Kent's decision R23 of 2026-09-21).

One route refreshes a quote — never on page load, never in a test, never in the build. **When it fails, the recorded quote stays and the card says the refresh failed**; the date on screen is still true. On the machine this was written on the refresh *will* fail, because the local resolver returns no address for the venue's hosts, which is why recorded-first is the rule rather than a fallback.

### B2 — A price you typed

A reader can type a price on any claim, on any map, with no venue and no key: *the best I can get is 41 cents* (**illustrative**). It is stamped `user`, dated, and printed as theirs; any edge against it carries *against a price you entered* on the same line. It does **not** fill the market chip on the tile, which says what a venue is charging (INV-11, three voices never merged).

### B3 — What the venue quotes, on the worked maps

Read from the venue on 2026-09-21 and saved raw; record 0020 has the detail. **Nothing quotes Brent crude**, so the curated map's Brent ending — and all eleven endings on the **recorded** map the walk opens — run on *no contract quotes this claim*, permanently.

The venue does quote the curated map's **hypothesis**, with the same deadline and a different resolution test. Kent's decision R30 takes that test as the map's own and adds one ending of kind `market` naming the contract, so the **curated** fixture carries exactly one comparable venue price. The **recorded** map is untouched until the one paid re-recording after the freeze.

### B4 — A market belief is a point, and the spread is a cost

Where a venue quotes a claim, the midpoint becomes the `market` belief on the tile. It has **no range**: the venue publishes no interval, so the low and high ends equal the number, and the chip says in words that no interval was published rather than implying certainty. What the two sides of the book differ by is what dealing costs, and it shows up in the buying and selling edges. Turning a spread into a range, as an earlier draft of this product did, produces a number nobody can trace to an input, a rule or a source.

### B5 — How a quote prints

Never as a bare number. The venue, the value, how we got it and the day are one unit, in one type size:

```
Polymarket · .07 · recorded 2026-09-21
```

That value is real — the midpoint of the Hormuz contract, read at 14:48 UTC on 2026-09-21. When likelihoods move to a percentage form a contract price will print the same way, and the card keeps saying which it is: **a price is not a probability**, even where the two read the same. One card line carries the caveat for all of them: *prices are as of the dates shown and were not refreshed; an edge against a stale quote is a stale edge.*

### B6 — A FRED figure is an observation

The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's economic-data service publishes measured historical levels — what a barrel actually settled at. That is a **spot anchor** for an ending that names an instrument, rendered with its series, its date, and the required line *"This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis."* It **never** fills the `market` belief slot.

---

## INVARIANTS

Written *for all inputs drawn from generator S, statement P holds*. This chapter owns `INV-thesis.4`–`INV-thesis.6`.

**INV-thesis.4 — No price arrives over a network in a test.** Over every test module in `backend/tests/`, run with outbound connections refused, the suite passes: the recorded loader reads the committed file, and the live adapter is exercised only against saved responses. **Tests:** `test_no_quote_test_touches_the_network`, `test_the_best_bid_is_the_last_bid`, `test_a_settled_market_is_read_from_its_flags`.

**INV-thesis.5 — Every rendered price says its venue, its source and its day.** For every quote from `quotes()`: the rendering used by the card, the tile chip and the export contains the venue (or, for a reader's own price, the words saying it is theirs), the source and the date. There is no path that renders a price alone. **Test:** `test_a_quote_prints_its_venue_source_and_day`, landing with the card, which is the first thing that renders.

**INV-thesis.6 — Only a venue's own number fills the market slot.** A new rule, not a refinement of INV-11. Over our own source, no function builds a `market` belief from a spot anchor or a `user` quote — a syntax-tree walk in the manner of `test_beliefs_never_merged`. Over generated data, for every `user` quote from `quotes()` and every anchor from `anchors()`, building the card leaves `beliefs.market` exactly as it was; and a belief built from a venue quote has its low and high ends equal to its midpoint. **Tests:** `test_a_fred_figure_never_fills_a_market_belief`, `test_a_reader_entered_price_is_not_a_market_belief`, `test_a_market_belief_has_no_invented_range`.

---

## ANTI-PATTERNS

1. **Do not fill an absent quote with a stand-in** — not a half, not the model's own number, not a blank chip. Because *no venue prices this* is a finding, and it drives a chain to an ending nobody can trade. **Instead:** the words *no market*, the reason beside them, and a break-even where one is defined.

2. **Do not read the price off the venue's display figure, or off the first line of the book.** Because the display figure is rounded and snaps to one and zero on a settled market, and bids come back ascending and offers descending, so the first is the *worst* — in the response saved for this chapter, `.01` against a best bid of `.06`. **Instead:** take the **best of each side by value** — the largest bid and the smallest offer, which is what *best* means and does not depend on the venue's ordering staying what it is today — derive the midpoint, and keep a saved response where the best and the first differ as a test. *(Built 2026-09-21: the first draft said "take the last of each side", which is the same answer on today's ordering and a wrong one the day it changes.)*

3. **Do not decide a market is live from its price**, because a settled market keeps serving a plausible book: read the closed and accepting-orders flags.

4. **Do not turn the spread into a range, and do not average two venues.** Because a bid–offer spread is what dealing costs rather than how unsure the venue is — and the venue publishes no interval at all — while two venues disagreeing is a signal the average destroys. **Instead:** a point belief with the cost in the edges, and one row per venue.

---

## Open questions

*Raised 2026-09-21.*

1. **What does dealing actually cost?** The fee schedule has not been read, so the fee is zero and the card says so.
2. **How stale is too stale?** The committed quote carries its day and the card says so, but nothing refuses a quote for being old.

*(Two questions this chapter used to raise were answered on 2026-09-21. Whether a dated quote file may be committed: it may, for research and development — Kent's decision R23; nobody has read the venue's terms of use, which is context and not a blocker. Which map carries a venue price: the curated one, under R30, written into B3 above.)*

"""Feed every raw Polymarket answer this repository saved through the new parser.

Run from the worktree's backend:

    cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend && \
      env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run --no-sync python \
      /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/06-1-review/venue_sweep.py

For every market in every saved file it builds the order book the market's own
best bid and best offer imply, and asks `quote_from` for a quote. What is counted:
what came back, and every kind of complaint, so that a crash with no sentence in
it stands out from a refusal that names its reason.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from katalyst.grounding import quote_from, read_book

SAVED = Path("/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/polymarket-look")


def events_in(parsed: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Every event object in one saved answer, whatever shape the file is."""
    if isinstance(parsed, list):
        return [one for one in parsed if isinstance(one, dict) and "markets" in one]
    if isinstance(parsed, dict):
        if "markets" in parsed:
            return [parsed]
        for value in parsed.values():
            if isinstance(value, list):
                inside = [one for one in value if isinstance(one, dict) and "markets" in one]
                if inside:
                    return inside
    return []


def a_book_for(market: dict[str, Any], token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The order book this market's own best bid and best offer imply."""
    return {
        "market": market.get("conditionId"),
        "asset_id": token,
        "timestamp": "1790002107921",
        "bids": [{"price": str(market.get("bestBid")), "size": "10"}],
        "asks": [{"price": str(market.get("bestAsk")), "size": "10"}],
        "tick_size": str(market.get("orderPriceMinTickSize") or "0.01"),
        "min_order_size": str(market.get("orderMinSize") or "5"),
    }


def main() -> None:
    outcomes_seen: Counter[str] = Counter()
    results: Counter[str] = Counter()
    complaints: Counter[str] = Counter()
    crashes: list[str] = []
    settled_read_as_live: list[str] = []
    markets = 0
    files = 0

    for file in sorted(SAVED.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        found = events_in(parsed)
        if not found:
            continue
        files += 1
        for event in found:
            for market in event.get("markets") or []:
                markets += 1
                raw = market.get("outcomes")
                try:
                    for one in json.loads(str(raw)):
                        outcomes_seen[str(one)] += 1
                except Exception:
                    outcomes_seen["<unreadable>"] += 1
                try:
                    tokens = json.loads(str(market.get("clobTokenIds")))
                except Exception:
                    tokens = []
                token = str(tokens[0]) if tokens else "no-token"
                try:
                    quote = quote_from(event, a_book_for(market, token), source="recorded")
                except ValueError as trouble:
                    results["refused with a sentence"] += 1
                    complaints[str(trouble)[:60]] += 1
                    continue
                except Exception as trouble:  # noqa: BLE001 - the point is to find these
                    results[f"CRASH {type(trouble).__name__}"] += 1
                    crashes.append(
                        f"{file.name} · market {market.get('id')} · "
                        f"{type(trouble).__name__}: {trouble}"
                    )
                    continue
                results["a quote"] += 1
                closed = bool(market.get("closed"))
                if closed and quote.live:
                    settled_read_as_live.append(str(market.get("id")))

    print(f"files with events: {files}   markets tried: {markets}\n")
    print("what came back:")
    for name, count in results.most_common():
        print(f"  {count:6d}  {name}")
    print("\nthe outcome names the venue uses, counted:")
    for name, count in outcomes_seen.most_common(14):
        print(f"  {count:6d}  {name!r}")
    print("\nthe complaints, by their first words:")
    for name, count in complaints.most_common(12):
        print(f"  {count:6d}  {name}")
    print(f"\ncrashes with no sentence in them: {len(crashes)}")
    for one in crashes[:25]:
        print(f"  {one}")
    print(f"\nsettled markets read as live: {len(settled_read_as_live)}")

    # The one real order book this repository saved, read again.
    committed = json.loads(
        Path(
            "/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend/recordings/quotes/"
            "3501950-2026-09-21.json"
        ).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )
    book = read_book(committed["book"])
    print(f"\nthe committed book: bid={book.bid} offer={book.offer} as_of={book.as_of.isoformat()}")
    print(f"  the venue's own stamp, in milliseconds: {committed['book']['timestamp']}")
    print(f"  the day in the file's name: 3501950-2026-09-21 · the day in the data: "
          f"{book.as_of.date().isoformat()}")

    # A one-sided book, an empty book, and a book whose prices are numbers not strings.
    for name, changed in (
        ("no bids", {"bids": []}),
        ("no asks", {"asks": []}),
        ("bids missing altogether", {"bids": None}),
        ("prices as numbers rather than strings", {"bids": [{"price": 0.06}]}),
        ("a timestamp in seconds rather than milliseconds", {"timestamp": "1790002107"}),
    ):
        try:
            read = read_book({**committed["book"], **changed})
            print(f"  {name}: bid={read.bid} offer={read.offer} as_of={read.as_of.isoformat()}")
        except Exception as trouble:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  {name}: {type(trouble).__name__}: {str(trouble)[:90]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

For every market in every saved file it builds the order book the market's own
best bid and best offer imply, and asks `quote_from` for a quote. What is counted:
what came back, and every kind of complaint, so that a crash with no sentence in
it stands out from a refusal that names its reason.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from katalyst.grounding import quote_from, read_book

SAVED = Path("/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/polymarket-look")


def events_in(parsed: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Every event object in one saved answer, whatever shape the file is."""
    if isinstance(parsed, list):
        return [one for one in parsed if isinstance(one, dict) and "markets" in one]
    if isinstance(parsed, dict):
        if "markets" in parsed:
            return [parsed]
        for value in parsed.values():
            if isinstance(value, list):
                inside = [one for one in value if isinstance(one, dict) and "markets" in one]
                if inside:
                    return inside
    return []


def a_book_for(market: dict[str, Any], token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The order book this market's own best bid and best offer imply."""
    return {
        "market": market.get("conditionId"),
        "asset_id": token,
        "timestamp": "1790002107921",
        "bids": [{"price": str(market.get("bestBid")), "size": "10"}],
        "asks": [{"price": str(market.get("bestAsk")), "size": "10"}],
        "tick_size": str(market.get("orderPriceMinTickSize") or "0.01"),
        "min_order_size": str(market.get("orderMinSize") or "5"),
    }


def main() -> None:
    outcomes_seen: Counter[str] = Counter()
    results: Counter[str] = Counter()
    complaints: Counter[str] = Counter()
    crashes: list[str] = []
    settled_read_as_live: list[str] = []
    markets = 0
    files = 0

    for file in sorted(SAVED.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        found = events_in(parsed)
        if not found:
            continue
        files += 1
        for event in found:
            for market in event.get("markets") or []:
                markets += 1
                raw = market.get("outcomes")
                try:
                    for one in json.loads(str(raw)):

    print("what came back:")
    for name, count in results.most_common():
        print(f"  {count:6d}  {name}")

    for name, count in outcomes_seen.most_common(14):

    for name, count in complaints.most_common(12):

            "3501950-2026-09-21.json"
        ).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )

    print(f"\nthe committed book: bid={book.bid} offer={book.offer} as_of={book.as_of.isoformat()}")
    print(f"  the venue's own stamp, in milliseconds: {committed['book']['timestamp']}")
    print(f"  the day in the file's name: 3501950-2026-09-21 · the day in the data: "
          f"{book.as_of.date().isoformat()}")

        ("no asks", {"asks": []}),

"""Does the outbound guard really stop a real fetch? Break it on purpose and watch.

The guard under review replaces three things on the `socket` module. This script
puts the same three in place by hand — it does not touch the worktree — and then
does what the venue adapter would really do: calls `urllib.request.urlopen`. It
also watches whether a name was looked up on the way, because a name lookup is
itself a call off this machine.

Run from the worktree's backend:

    cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend && \
      env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run --no-sync python \
      /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/06-1-review/guard_teeth.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import socket
import urllib.request
from typing import Any, NoReturn


class WentOutbound(RuntimeError):
    """A test tried to open a connection to somewhere outside this machine."""


def refuse(*_arguments: Any, **_named: Any) -> NoReturn:
    raise WentOutbound("refused")


names_looked_up: list[str] = []
real_getaddrinfo = socket.getaddrinfo


def watched_getaddrinfo(host: Any, port: Any, *rest: Any, **named: Any) -> Any:
    names_looked_up.append(str(host))
    return real_getaddrinfo(host, port, *rest, **named)


def main() -> None:
    socket.getaddrinfo = watched_getaddrinfo  # type: ignore[assignment]
    socket.socket.connect = refuse  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    socket.socket.connect_ex = refuse  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    socket.create_connection = refuse  # type: ignore[assignment]

    print("the three the guard replaces are in place.\n")

    for address in ("http://gamma-api.polymarket.com/events?slug=x",):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(address, timeout=2) as answer:
                print(f"  {address}: ANSWERED {answer.status} — the guard did not stop it")
        except WentOutbound:
            print(f"  {address}: refused by the guard")
        except Exception as trouble:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  {address}: {type(trouble).__name__}: {str(trouble)[:120]}")
            cause = trouble
            while getattr(cause, "__cause__", None) or getattr(cause, "__context__", None):
                cause = cause.__cause__ or cause.__context__
                if isinstance(cause, WentOutbound):
                    print("      …and underneath it, the guard refused")
                    break
                if cause is None:
                    break

    print(f"\nnames looked up on the way out: {names_looked_up}")
    print("(a name lookup is itself a question asked of a machine that is not this one)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

=== 76119b6 spec(thesis): three things the chapters left to the keyboard, written back
Building 06-1 settled three details the chapters stated loosely, and a chapter
is kept true rather than left to drift.

`edge.md` — a break-even goes with a contract and with nothing else, which is
one rule rather than a row-by-row answer and agrees with every row of the table
already there. The mixture needs a third world and so appears only when the
caller hands one in; the chapter now says why the alternative is not available,
which is that the arithmetic recovering it assumes the equality the passage
three lines above says does not hold. And `priced` may be told two further
things — the fee, and that other world — neither of which can be handed in
instead of a world.

`quotes.md` — the anti-pattern said "take the last of each side" of an order
book. That is the right answer on today's ordering and a wrong one the day it
changes, so it now says to take the best of each side by value, which is what
*best* means.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>


=== 9715dd2 test(backend): the two new layers may read down the stack, and never up
The check that reads our own import lines now walks three directories instead
of one, and the order they may depend in runs one way only. The rules layer
gains `katalyst.thesis` on its forbidden list. The layer that fetches prices may
read the rules layer — a price becomes a likelihood on a claim — and nothing
above it. The layer that turns a map into a trade may read both of those, which
are exactly the two things an edge is made of, and serves nothing, fetches
nothing and asks nobody.

One thing is deliberately allowed where it is forbidden everywhere else: the
standard library's way of opening a connection, inside the price-fetching layer
alone, which is the one layer permitted to reach a venue.

And a fourth test, because a boundary check pointed at an empty directory passes
for the wrong reason: each of the three directories is confirmed to have files
in it for the check to read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>


=== becf8a9 feat(thesis): an edge is read from the world nothing was supposed in, against the price you would pay
The reader's first finance question is *what is already priced in?* `priced` is
the only thing that answers it, and the only way an `Edge` is built. Two traps
are closed by its shape rather than by a caller's care.

**Which world.** *Suppose this is true* re-works the map, so a tile then answers
*the chance of this in a world where the strait has been made to open* — and a
venue's price answers the old question. So the function takes two worlds and
both are required: a caller holding only the world on screen cannot write the
mistake down, and the compared number is always read from the untouched one.
Either button refuses — supposing and reporting alike, one conservative rule
(R20) — and the cost is said out loud in the sentence the card prints.

**Which price.** You buy at the offer and sell at the bid, so there are two
edges and the venue's fee is the only cost term. No half-the-spread anywhere:
the spread is already inside the two prices. The midpoint is shown because a
reader recognises it and is never traded against.

# Read-only review of 06-1 — *the quote and the edge*

**Branch** `feat/06-quote`, worktree `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote`, four commits on `adr/06-the-trade` · **reviewed 2026-09-22 by RB6** · nothing in the worktree was changed.

Every script quoted below is in `plans/analysis/scripts/06-1-review/` and prints the numbers this page quotes. To re-run any of them:

```
cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend
env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run --no-sync python \
  /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/scripts/06-1-review/<name>.py
```

`repro.py` needs `PYTHONPATH=/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-06-quote/backend` as well, because it draws from `tests/strategies.py`. `mutants.sh` is run with `bash` and copies the branch into the scratch directory before breaking anything.

The arithmetic of the seven-row table is **right on the yes side** and I checked every row by hand. The three things below are not small.

---

## Must fix before the pull request opens

### MF-1 — A contract ending on the **no** side is priced against the wrong number, and names the opposite side of the trade

`backend/src/katalyst/thesis/edge.py:379-380`

```python
buying=model.p - quote.offer - fee,
selling=quote.bid - model.p - fee,
```

`priced` never reads `ContractPayoff.side` (`domain/proposition.py:182`) and never reads `Quote.side` (`grounding/quote.py:160`). `Quote.side` exists for exactly this reason — its own description says *"the same contract reads .07 on one side and .93 on the other"* — and nothing consults it.

A claim's number is *the chance the claim comes true*. An ending whose payoff says `side="no"` makes money when the claim **fails**, and the NO outcome token is a separate order book that pays one dollar in that case. The number to set a NO price against is therefore `1 − the claim's number`. Subtracting a NO price from the claim's own number is a comparison between two different questions — the very mistake record 0018 exists to prevent, one layer down from the one it caught.

**Reproduction** — `table_by_hand.py`, section 6:

```
no-side ending: the model says the claim is 0.35515073500573635 true, so 0.6448492649942636 false.
the NO token — which pays when the claim fails — is offered at 0.6 and bid at 0.58.
by hand: buying it is worth 0.04484926499426367, selling it -0.06484926499426369  -> BUY
`priced` says: buying -0.24484926499426363, selling 0.2248492649942636  -> SELL
FAIL  no side: the edge of buying is worked out on the side that was priced
FAIL  no side: the two answers name the same side of the trade
```

It does not merely get the size wrong. It tells the reader to **sell at .58** where the honest answer is **buy at .60**.

Two more holes in the same place, from the same script:

```
FAIL  a quote for the other side of the contract is refused: got False, wanted True
FAIL  a quote for another market is refused: got False, wanted True
```

Nothing checks that the quote handed in is even **about this claim's contract**: a quote carrying `market_id="7654321"` prices a claim whose payoff names `contract_id="3501950"`, silently. That is a number on a card that cannot be traced to its source, which is the second veto.

**Is it reachable?** Yes, and about half the time. The model may propose either side — `engine/proposal.py:276-285` hands the whole `Payoff` union to the model — and the generator already draws both: `repro.py`, section 3, over 200 drawn maps:

```
contract endings on the yes side: 50;  on the no side: 43;  instrument endings: 120
```

The two property tests that price a generated map (`tests/thesis/test_edge.py:246`, `:348`) hand **every** one of those a quote built with `side="yes"` (`agreeing_quote`, `test_edge.py:132`), and `test_agreeing_with_the_market_reads_exactly_zero` then asserts the answer is exactly nothing. On a no-side ending it is exactly nothing and exactly wrong. There is no test anywhere on this branch with a no-side payoff: `A_CONTRACT` (`test_edge.py:176`) is the only contract in the file and it is `side="yes"`.

**The fix, in words.** Smallest honest version, all inside `priced`, no record change:

1. When the claim's payoff is a `ContractPayoff` and a quote is handed in, **require that the quote is about that contract and that side** — `quote.market_id == payoff.contract_id`, `quote.venue == payoff.venue`, `quote.side == payoff.side` — and raise `ValueError` when not, the way a claim that is not on the map already does at `edge.py:349`. It is a broken promise between our own pieces of code, not something a reader did, and the existing precedent covers it exactly.
2. Compute the compared number as `model.p` on a yes-side payoff and `1 - model.p` on a no-side one, and run the **same** flip through `BreakEven` and through `_sign_changes_across_the_range`, whose `model.lo`/`model.hi` become `1 - hi` / `1 - lo`. A NO position's break-even is `(1 − model) ∓ fee`, not `model ∓ fee`.
3. If (2) is judged too much for this pull request, then refuse a no-side payoff **by name** rather than pricing it wrongly, and say so in the table — but (1) is not optional either way.

`spec/thesis/edge.md`'s decision table and the chapter's *arithmetic* section owe one row and one sentence for whichever is chosen; the table is billed as *total* and today it is silent on half the contract endings this product can generate. A user-typed quote (`source="user"`, no side at all) needs a row too: today it is accepted and treated as a yes.

---

### MF-2 — `quote_from` raises a bare `KeyError` on ordinary real venue answers, including the repository's own saved settled-market response

`backend/src/katalyst/grounding/polymarket.py:215,218,219`

```python
ends=date.fromisoformat(str(market["endDateIso"])),
...
resting=float(market["liquidityNum"]),
traded=float(market["volumeNum"]),
```

Its docstring (`polymarket.py:193-197`) promises `Raises: ValueError:` for three named cases. It also raises `KeyError`, with no sentence in it, on fields the venue simply omits.

**Reproduction** — `venue_shapes.py`, over every raw response saved in `plans/analysis/scripts/polymarket-look/`, 1 693 distinct real markets:

```
fields the parser indexes that are ABSENT, counted:
     189  volumeNum
     154  liquidityNum
      24  endDateIso
```

and `venue_sweep.py`, feeding each of them through `quote_from`:

```
markets tried: 2332
    1388  a quote
     773  refused with a sentence
     171  CRASH KeyError
  event-wti-september-2026.json · market 3866513 · KeyError: 'liquidityNum'
  search-active-Brent-crude.json · market 3365472 · KeyError: 'endDateIso'
  ...
```

The sharpest instance: **market 3866513 is the settled market this branch committed as a test fixture**, `backend/tests/grounding/responses/settled-market.json`. `repro.py`, section 1:

```
'liquidityNum' in the saved market record: False
quote_from: KeyError: 'liquidityNum'
```

So the one *settled market* row of the decision table can never be reached from the real answer the branch saved for it. `test_a_settled_market_is_read_from_its_flags` (`tests/grounding/test_polymarket.py:75`) works around this by `model_copy`-ing two flags and two prices onto the **Hormuz** quote. The row is exercised against an assembled object, never against the venue answer that made the row necessary.

Two consequences beyond the crash:

* `refresh` catches everything (`polymarket.py:264`) and reports the failure as *"Polymarket could not be read just now (KeyError)"* — the venue answered perfectly well; we could not read it. A sentence that names the wrong party is worse than no sentence.
* `recorded.py:147` catches `KeyError` and wraps it, so the committed-file path is safe by luck rather than by contract; `quote_from` is public API (`grounding/__init__.py`) and a direct caller gets the bare error.

**The fix, in words.** Read the three optional fields with `.get`, treat absent as absent — `resting` and `traded` are already `float | None` on `Quote` — and let `ends` be `None` when the venue gives no `endDateIso`, since `Quote.ends` is optional too. `Quote`'s validator then has to stop demanding those three of a venue quote (`quote.py:59-73`): the rule it wants is *a venue quote names its venue, its three identifiers and its side*, not *the venue filled in every optional field*. One rule over two: "what only a venue can tell us" and "what a venue always tells us" are different lists and the file uses one list for both. Keep `question`, `rules`, `conditionId`, `id`, `closed`, `acceptingOrders`, `outcomes` and `clobTokenIds` as hard requirements, because every one of the 1 693 markets has them (measured, `venue_shapes.py`), and refuse by name if one is missing.

---

### MF-3 — The mixture reads the supposed claim's own tile number, which the rules layer says no surface may print — and then manufactures the exact identity record 0018 says it must never claim

`backend/src/katalyst/thesis/edge.py:456-458`

```python
reading_supposed=shown.beliefs[claim].p,
reading_otherwise=otherwise.beliefs[claim].p,
```

`World`'s own docstring (`domain/propagation.py:200-204`) is explicit: *"A claim whose supposition is holding reads 1 — exactly 1, range and all, or 0 when it was supposed false. That number is there so that a chain of claims multiplied together has a factor for it, and for nothing else: **no surface may print it.** Every reader looks at `states` first."* `_mixture_of` never looks at `states`.

When the reader supposes the **ending being priced** — which is exactly what `test_an_edge_reads_the_unsupposed_world` does at `test_edge.py:260-268` — the mixture carries 1.0 and 0.0, and the two terms then weigh to the base number **exactly**, by arithmetic and not by explanation.

**Reproduction** — the snippet in `repro-notes` form, run against the branch:

```
the reader supposed the very ending being priced.
  reading_supposed  = 1.0
  reading_otherwise = 0.0
  weight_supposed   = 0.4725367547944188
  the state the domain records for that claim on its own day: supposed
  the mixture works out to 0.4725367547944188 against the base number 0.4725367547944188
```

(the five lines are produced by the inline script at the foot of this file; it uses `table_by_hand.py`'s map.)

A card printing that shows a reader two numbers it is forbidden to show and a perfect agreement that means nothing. Record 0018 spends a page on *the terms are an explanation with a measured residual, not an identity* — and the one input that makes it an identity is unguarded.

**The fix, in words.** `_mixture_of` refuses when the supposition is on the claim being explained: return `None`, because a mixture of *the ending supposed true* against *the ending supposed false* explains nothing about the ending. Three lines, beside the two checks already there. While in the file, say in the docstring that the readings are read from `beliefs` and are therefore only meaningful for a claim that is **not** the supposed one — the reason `states` exists.

---

## Should fix

1. **`UNKNOWN_FEE = 0.0` as a default flatters every edge, and nothing carries "unknown".** `edge.py:63,295`. Record 0018 and the chapter both say *"the card says the fee is unknown"* — but `Edge.fee` is a bare `float`, so a card cannot tell an unknown fee from a fee somebody read and found to be zero, except by comparing against a sentinel that is itself `0.0`. **Smallest honest design:** `fee: float | None = None` on `priced` and on `Edge`; the arithmetic uses `fee or 0.0`; `None` *is* the state, the card branches on it, and `UNKNOWN_FEE` disappears. That is one field and no new concept, and it makes the record's promise expressible from the value instead of from a comment. Requiring the fee outright is the other defensible answer and costs every call site an argument nobody can fill honestly yet; I prefer `None`.

### MF-1 — A contract ending on the **no** side is priced against the wrong number, and names the opposite side of the trade

`backend/src/katalyst/thesis/edge.py:379-380`

```python
buying=model.p - quote.offer - fee,
selling=quote.bid - model.p - fee,
```

`priced` never reads `ContractPayoff.side` (`domain/proposition.py:182`) and never reads `Quote.side` (`grounding/quote.py:160`). `Quote.side` exists for exactly this reason — its own description says *"the same contract reads .07 on one side and .93 on the other"* — and nothing consults it.

A claim's number is *the chance the claim comes true*. An ending whose payoff says `side="no"` makes money when the claim **fails**, and the NO outcome token is a separate order book that pays one dollar in that case. The number to set a NO price against is therefore `1 − the claim's number`. Subtracting a NO price from the claim's own number is a comparison between two different questions — the very mistake record 0018 exists to prevent, one layer down from the one it caught.

**Reproduction** — `table_by_hand.py`, section 6:

```
no-side ending: the model says the claim is 0.35515073500573635 true, so 0.6448492649942636 false.
the NO token — which pays when the claim fails — is offered at 0.6 and bid at 0.58.
by hand: buying it is worth 0.04484926499426367, selling it -0.06484926499426369  -> BUY
`priced` says: buying -0.24484926499426363, selling 0.2248492649942636  -> SELL
FAIL  no side: the edge of buying is worked out on the side that was priced
FAIL  no side: the two answers name the same side of the trade
```

It does not merely get the size wrong. It tells the reader to **sell at .58** where the honest answer is **buy at .60**.

Two more holes in the same place, from the same script:

```
FAIL  a quote for the other side of the contract is refused: got False, wanted True
FAIL  a quote for another market is refused: got False, wanted True
```

Nothing checks that the quote handed in is even **about this claim's contract**: a quote carrying `market_id="7654321"` prices a claim whose payoff names `contract_id="3501950"`, silently. That is a number on a card that cannot be traced to its source, which is the second veto.

**Is it reachable?** Yes, and about half the time. The model may propose either side — `engine/proposal.py:276-285` hands the whole `Payoff` union to the model — and the generator already draws both: `repro.py`, section 3, over 200 drawn maps:

```
contract endings on the yes side: 50;  on the no side: 43;  instrument endings: 120
```

The two property tests that price a generated map (`tests/thesis/test_edge.py:246`, `:348`) hand **every** one of those a quote built with `side="yes"` (`agreeing_quote`, `test_edge.py:132`), and `test_agreeing_with_the_market_reads_exactly_zero` then asserts the answer is exactly nothing. **The fix, in words.** Smallest honest version, all inside `priced`, no record change:

1. When the claim's payoff is a `ContractPayoff` and a quote is handed in, **require that the quote is about that contract and that side** — `quote.market_id == payoff.contract_id`, `quote.venue == payoff.venue`, `quote.side == payoff.side` — and raise `ValueError` when not, the way a claim that is not on the map already does at `edge.py:349`. It is a broken promise between our own pieces of code, not something a reader did, and the existing precedent covers it exactly.
2. Compute the compared number as `model.p` on a yes-side payoff and `1 - model.p` on a no-side one, and run the **same** flip through `BreakEven` and through `_sign_changes_across_the_range`, whose `model.lo`/`model.hi` become `1 - hi` / `1 - lo`. A claim's number is *the chance the claim comes true*. An ending whose payoff says `side="no"` makes money when the claim **fails**, and the NO outcome token is a separate order book that pays one dollar in that case. The number to set a NO price against is therefore `1 − the claim's number`. Subtracting a NO price from the claim's own number is a comparison between two different questions — the very mistake record 0018 exists to prevent, one layer down from the one it caught.

**Reproduction** — `table_by_hand.py`, section 6:

by hand: buying it is worth 0.04484926499426367, selling it -0.06484926499426369  -> BUY
`priced` says: buying -0.24484926499426363, selling 0.2248492649942636  -> SELL
FAIL  no side: the edge of buying is worked out on the side that was priced
FAIL  no side: the two answers name the same side of the trade

FAIL  a quote for another market is refused: got False, wanted True

1. **`UNKNOWN_FEE = 0.0` as a default flatters every edge, and nothing carries "unknown".** `edge.py:63,295`.
